questions.prompt: What fundamental NTLM design flaw does relay actually exploit?
options: NTLM hashes are stored in plaintext
NTLM authentication was never designed to bind a session to a specific destination, only to prove who's authenticating
NTLM requires no authentication at all
NTLM only works over unencrypted connections
questions.explanation: The core flaw is that NTLM doesn't bind authentication to a specific destination — an attacker in the middle can forward a real authentication attempt to a different target entirely.

questions.prompt: What two controls, enforced domain-wide, make the relay chain fail at its final step regardless of how successful poisoning or coercion was?
options: SMB signing and LDAP signing plus channel binding
questions.explanation: Signing enforcement is the durable fix — without it, a relayed authentication attempt is accepted as valid; with it enforced, the relay fails at the final step no matter how the authentication was captured.

questions.prompt: What does Responder specifically exploit to capture authentication attempts?
options: A vulnerability in TLS certificate validation
Broadcast name-resolution fallback protocols (LLMNR, NBT-NS, mDNS) when normal DNS resolution fails
A flaw in Kerberos ticket encryption
questions.explanation: Responder poisons LLMNR/NBT-NS/mDNS broadcast fallback queries — when a host's normal name lookup fails, it broadcasts and Responder simply answers, capturing the resulting authentication attempt.

questions.prompt: How can a successful LDAP relay chain connect directly to the RBCD attack path from the previous lesson?
options: It can't — they're entirely unrelated techniques
LDAP relay can be used to directly write msDS-AllowedToActOnBehalfOfOtherIdentity on a target computer object
LDAP relay only works against DNS servers
questions.explanation: A relayed LDAP authentication with sufficient rights can configure RBCD directly — meaning a relay chain can end in the same privilege-escalation outcome as RBCD, with no separate credential-theft step.
